Jupyter Integration

Install Blog GitHub

Jupyter: Interactive Gollek Development

The Gollek Jupyter integration is a standalone Java kernel built on JShell. It preloads the common Gollek ML classes, renders rich notebook outputs, and adds a small magic-command layer so notebook users can inspect artifacts without dropping into a terminal.

Use this path when you want a notebook workflow that feels close to Python Jupyter, but keeps the implementation in Java/Gollek.

1. Prerequisites

  • Java 25 or the Java version used by your local Gollek checkout.
  • Python 3 with Jupyter Notebook or JupyterLab installed.
  • A local Gollek repository checkout.

You do not need to install IJava separately. The Gollek kernel ships its own kernel spec and launcher.

2. Build, Doctor, And Install

Run the kernel build from the Gollek repository:

cd gollek/integration/jupyter/gollek-jupyter-kernel
./rebuild_kernel.sh local-fat
python3 install.py --dry-run --user
python3 doctor.py
python3 install.py --user

Then start Jupyter:

jupyter lab

Create a notebook with the Gollek (Java 25 + AI/ML) kernel.

3. First Notebook Cells

The kernel starts with common imports and helper functions already loaded:

gollekHelp()

gollekTensorDemo()

gollekPreviewTensorDemo()

gollekModelSummary()

For a simple model cell:

var model = new Sequential(new Linear(2, 3), new ReLU());
model

4. Notebook Magics

Discover the available notebook commands from inside the notebook:

%magics
%help %du
%pwd
%tree
%du .

Useful day-to-day commands:

Group Commands Use
Discovery %magics, %help <magic> Learn the kernel surface from the notebook.
Session %reset, %time <expr>, %timeit [-n N] <expr> Recover state and benchmark cells.
Workspace %pwd, %cd <PATH>, %ls, %tree [PATH], %du [PATH] Navigate and inspect project folders.
Files %cat, %head, %tail, %grep, %findfile, %wc, %diff, %sha256 Preview, search, compare, and verify artifacts.
Formats %json, %csv [-n N] [--profile], %tsv [-n N] [--profile], %sample [--tsv] [-n N] [--seed S], %sort [--tsv] [-n N] [--desc], %filter [--tsv] [-n N], %describe [--tsv], %schema [--tsv], %missing [--tsv], %valuecounts [--tsv] [--top N], %groupby [--tsv], %corr [--tsv] [--heatmap], %scatter [--tsv], %lineplot [--tsv], %hist [--tsv] [--bins N], %md, %html, %yaml, %toml, %xml, %ini, %properties, %envfile Render common data/config formats, random samples, sorted and filtered row previews, numeric summaries, schema inference, missingness checks, categorical counts, grouped summaries, correlation matrices, and quick plots in notebook output.
Archives %zipls, %zipcat, %tarls, %tarcat, %extract Inspect and extract selected bundle entries.
Dependencies %classpath, %addjar, %maven, %deps, %whichclass, %env Inspect and extend the live notebook runtime.

5. Artifact Inspection Example

This workflow is useful for generated reports, model bundles, and downloaded datasets:

%zipls bundle.zip
%zipcat bundle.zip nested/report.txt
%tarls bundle.tar.gz
%tarcat bundle.tar.gz nested/report.txt
%extract --dry-run bundle.tar.gz nested/report.txt extracted/report.txt
%extract bundle.tar.gz nested/report.txt extracted/report.txt
%sha256 bundle.tar.gz
%du extracted

%extract writes only one selected archive entry into the notebook working directory, refuses overwrites, and supports --dry-run so the path can be checked before writing.

6. Dataframe-Style Preview Example

Use -n to control preview rows and --profile to add lightweight column stats:

%csv -n 20 --profile metrics.csv
%tsv -n 20 --profile features.tsv
%sample -n 5 --seed 42 metrics.csv
%sample --tsv -n 5 features.tsv
%sort -n 10 --desc metrics.csv score
%sort --tsv -n 10 features.tsv latency
%filter -n 10 metrics.csv score >= 0.8
%filter --tsv features.tsv status == ok
%describe metrics.csv
%describe --tsv features.tsv
%schema metrics.csv
%schema --tsv features.tsv
%missing metrics.csv
%missing --tsv features.tsv
%valuecounts metrics.csv label
%valuecounts --tsv --top 10 features.tsv status
%groupby metrics.csv label
%groupby metrics.csv label score mean
%groupby --tsv features.tsv status latency sum
%corr metrics.csv
%corr --tsv features.tsv
%corr --heatmap metrics.csv
%scatter metrics.csv weight height
%scatter --tsv features.tsv step accuracy
%lineplot metrics.csv epoch loss
%lineplot --tsv features.tsv step accuracy
%hist --bins 12 metrics.csv loss
%hist --tsv --bins 12 features.tsv accuracy

The preview reports total rows, visible preview rows, column count, truncation, and optional non-empty, missing, numeric, min, max, and mean stats per column. %sample adds random row sampling for quick spot checks, with --seed support for reproducible notebook output. %sort adds top/bottom row previews by one CSV or TSV column. Numeric columns sort numerically when possible, and blank values stay at the end. %filter adds quick row subsets by one CSV or TSV column, including equality, numeric comparisons, text predicates, and blank/notblank checks. %describe adds pandas-style numeric summaries: count, missing, mean, standard deviation, min, p25, median, p75, and max. %schema adds dtype-style inference for empty, boolean, integer, decimal, date, datetime, and text columns, plus examples and missing counts. %missing adds a pandas-style missingness check with missing counts, present counts, percentages, and an inline SVG bar chart by column. %valuecounts adds pandas-style categorical counts with percentages, an inline SVG bar chart, and explicit (blank) handling for missing values. %groupby adds pandas-style grouped summaries: counts by group, or numeric sum, mean, min, and max over a selected value column. %corr adds a Pearson correlation matrix for numeric columns and computes each cell pairwise from rows where both columns are numeric. Add --heatmap for a blue-to-red inline SVG heatmap above the matrix table. %scatter turns paired numeric columns into an inline SVG relationship check and reports rows skipped because either axis was blank or non-numeric. %lineplot turns one numeric Y column into an inline SVG trend chart with the X column used as point labels. %hist turns one numeric column into an inline SVG distribution view and reports skipped non-numeric or blank values.

7. API Specification

The public notebook surface is documented in the gollek-integration-jupyter API reference. Use that page as the command contract for helpers, magics, MIME outputs, dependency loading, and archive/artifact behavior.
